commands.step: Lockfile-drift gate — install (Node 22, non-Dependabot only; D4B-002 + FT-a)
commands.text:
set +e
npm install --package-lock-only --no-audit --no-fund 2> install.log
install_exit=$?
set -e
if [ $install_exit -ne 0 ]; then
  # D4B-001: classify the failure. Network-class failures get a
  # warning + a non-blocking skip; everything else is a hard
  # error so an operator never confuses "lockfile mismatch" with
  # "registry was down".
  if grep -E -i "ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|ENETUNREACH|ENOTFOUND|EAI_AGAIN|socket hang up|network timeout|registry\.npmjs\.org.*5[0-9][0-9]|ERR_SOCKET_TIMEOUT" install.log >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "::warning::lockfile-drift gate skipped: 'npm install --package-lock-only' hit a transient network error. Lockfile NOT checked this run. Re-run if a drift was actually expected."
    echo "skipped=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::lockfile-drift gate failed: 'npm install --package-lock-only' exited non-zero with a non-network error. Install log:"
  cat install.log
  exit 1
fi
echo "skipped=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

commands.step: Atlas diff on this pull request
commands.text:
marker='<!-- atlas-diff -->'
delta="$RUNNER_TEMP/atlas-diff.md"
body="$RUNNER_TEMP/atlas-diff-comment.md"
depth=()
if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = "true" ]; then depth=(--depth=1); fi
if ! git fetch --no-tags "${depth[@]}" origin "+refs/heads/${BASE_REF}:refs/remotes/origin/${BASE_REF}"; then
  echo "::warning::atlas diff skipped: origin/${BASE_REF} could not be fetched"
  exit 0
fi
if ! node packages/atlas/cli.js diff --base "origin/${BASE_REF}" > "$delta"; then
  cat "$delta"
  echo "::warning::atlas diff did not run against origin/${BASE_REF}; no comment posted"
  exit 0
fi
cat "$delta"
cat "$delta" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
{ printf '%s\n' "$marker"; cat "$delta"; } > "$body"
if [ "$HEAD_REPO" != "$REPO" ]; then
  echo "::notice::pull request from a fork: its token cannot comment, so the delta is in this log and the job summary"
  exit 0
fi
ids=$(gh api --paginate "repos/${REPO}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments" \
  --jq ".[] | select(.user.login == \"github-actions[bot]\" and (.body | contains(\"${marker}\"))) | .id") || ids=''
id="${ids%%$'\n'*}"
if [ -n "$id" ]; then
  gh api --method PATCH "repos/${REPO}/issues/comments/${id}" -F "body=@${body}" > /dev/null \
    || echo "::warning::atlas diff comment ${id} could not be updated; the delta is in this log"
else
  gh api --method POST "repos/${REPO}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments" -F "body=@${body}" > /dev/null \
    || echo "::warning::atlas diff comment could not be posted; the delta is in this log"
fi
exit 0
npm run test:scripts
npm test
npm ci
node --test scripts/check-step-fixtures.test.mjs
npm ci
npm run build

# Defensive guard: surface a clear error if the dispatcher sent no
# submission payload (CI-B-002). The downstream verify pipeline
# rejects null gracefully but produces no GitHub error annotation,
# so an operator debugging a misbehaving consumer dispatcher would
# otherwise see only a green workflow with a silent rejection record.
if [ -z "$SUBMISSION_PAYLOAD" ] || [ "$SUBMISSION_PAYLOAD" = "null" ]; then
  echo "::error::repository_dispatch received with missing/null client_payload.submission. Consumer dispatcher is misconfigured — check the dispatching workflow's dogfood.yml step."
  exit 1
fi
# d6-infra-B001: decouple run.js's exit code from the step's success.
# run.js exits 1 for a REJECTED submission (verification.status !==
# 'accepted') — a NORMAL, designed outcome: the rejection record is
# written to records/_rejected/ and MUST be committed. Only exit >=2
# is a genuine pipeline fault. The default shell is
# `bash -eo pipefail`, so without this `set +e` the `node ... | tee`
# pipeline propagates exit 1 and `set -e` halts the job at this step,
# skipping 'Read result' + 'Commit' and silently dropping the
# _rejected evidence the system exists to accumulate. `tee`'s own exit
# is masked by PIPESTATUS so a write hiccup can't hide node's code.
# PB-CI-003: capture run.js's STDERR to a file as well. run.js emits
# its staleness signal (a "failed_stage":"rebuild_indexes" NDJSON
# event + a "may be stale" console.error) on STDERR when a record
# persists but the index rebuild throws — it still returns
# written:true/accepted, so the stdout result JSON (captured by tee
# below) carries NO staleness field. Without capturing stderr the
# degraded run is invisible.
# F-50558cb2: plain redirect + post-pipeline cat, NOT a tee process
# substitution. Bash does not wait for a process substitution
# when the pipeline completes, so the step could exit while tee's
# final flush was in flight and the 'Warn on stale indexes' step
# would read a truncated capture — silently skipping the degraded-run
# warning this capture exists to feed. The redirect is complete
# before cat replays it to the live log, and stderr is not a
# pipeline element so PIPESTATUS is unchanged.
set +e
echo "$SUBMISSION_PAYLOAD" | node packages/ingest/run.js --provenance=github 2> /tmp/ingest-stderr.log | tee /tmp/ingest-result.json
rc=${PIPESTATUS[1]}
set -e
cat /tmp/ingest-stderr.log >&2
# F-42e57a77: DEFER the red run past the commit step. run.js's
# generic catch exits 2 for anything thrown inside ingest() — which
# can fire AFTER a record was persisted to the runner working tree
# (persist-then-fail-later is a proven run.js shape; the stale-index
# path is the precedent). Exiting here would skip the commit step
# and discard that evidence with the runner — the same evidence-loss
# class F-caeeacc3 closed for the parse seam. Annotate the fault,
# record fault=$rc, and let the 'Fail run on deferred pipeline
# fault' step red the run AFTER the evidence is committed.
if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then
  echo "::error::ingest pipeline faulted (exit $rc) on a repository_dispatch submission — this is a genuine error, NOT a rejection (rejections exit 1 and still commit). Inspect the run log above and the structured \"stage\":\"error\" NDJSON event from packages/ingest/run.js. Any evidence run.js persisted before the fault is still committed below; the run fails at the deferred-fault step."
  echo "fault=$rc" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  exit 0
fi
# exit 0 (accepted) or 1 (rejected) both proceed: the accepted or
# _rejected record is on the runner working tree and must be committed.

# d6-infra-B001: same rejected-exit decouple as the repository_dispatch
# leg. run.js exits 1 on a rejected submission (the _rejected record is
# written and must still be committed); only exit >=2 is a real fault.
# PB-CI-003: capture run.js STDERR (same rationale as the
# repository_dispatch leg) so a stale-index degraded run is detectable.
# F-50558cb2: plain redirect + post-pipeline cat, not a procsub —
# see the repository_dispatch leg for the torn-capture rationale.
set +e
node packages/ingest/run.js --provenance=github --file "$SUBMISSION_FILE" 2> /tmp/ingest-stderr.log | tee /tmp/ingest-result.json
rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e
cat /tmp/ingest-stderr.log >&2
# F-42e57a77: same fault-defer as the repository_dispatch leg — see
# that leg's comment for the persist-then-fault evidence-loss rationale.
if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then
  echo "::error::ingest pipeline faulted (exit $rc) on workflow_dispatch file $SUBMISSION_FILE — genuine error, NOT a rejection (rejections exit 1 and still commit). Inspect the run log above and the structured \"stage\":\"error\" NDJSON event from packages/ingest/run.js. Any evidence run.js persisted before the fault is still committed below; the run fails at the deferred-fault step."
  echo "fault=$rc" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  exit 0
fi

if [ -f /tmp/ingest-result.json ]; then
  # d6-infra-B003: parse-guard before extracting fields. The `[ -f ]`
  # check above covers an ABSENT file but not a MALFORMED one — if a
  # future change emits a non-JSON warning to stdout, or a tee is torn
  # by a crash mid-write, `jq -r '.status'` exits non-zero and `set -e`
  # fails the step with jq's terse parse error instead of an
  # operator-legible annotation naming the run. Validate parseability
  # first and emit a structured ::error:: (matching the
  # SUBMISSION_PAYLOAD null-guard and the rebase ::error:: discipline
  # elsewhere in this file).
  # F-caeeacc3: DEFER the failure instead of exiting 1 here. run.js
  # already persisted the accepted or _rejected record to the runner
  # working tree; a red step between persist and commit skips the
  # commit step and discards that evidence with the run (the
  # repository_dispatch payload is unrecoverable). Flag
  # parse_failed=true so the commit step still runs, then the
  # 'Fail run on deferred result-parse error' step reds the run
  # AFTER the evidence is committed.
  if ! jq -e . /tmp/ingest-result.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "::error::ingest-result.json is not valid JSON — packages/ingest/run.js emitted unparseable stdout (a non-JSON warning, or a torn write). Raw contents follow; fix run.js's stdout contract so it always emits a single JSON object on the result line. The working-tree evidence is still committed below; the run fails at the deferred-error step."
    cat /tmp/ingest-result.json
    echo "parse_failed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    exit 0
  fi
  # `// empty` so an absent field yields '' rather than the literal
  # string 'null' leaking into the step outputs.
  # F-b68c7e52: `tr -d '\n\r'` at extraction, not just `// empty`.
  # These three values are read from run.js's stdout, which is
  # derived from untrusted repository_dispatch client_payload — a
  # newline embedded in run_id (or status/written) would let the
  # single-line `key=value` GITHUB_OUTPUT form parse every line
  # after the first as an ADDITIONAL step output (GitHub's
  # documented output-injection class), letting a crafted value
  # forge/suppress the badge-regen, commit, and deferred-fail
  # gates below that key off these outputs. persist.js's
  # /^[\w-]+$/ run_id guard makes this unreachable today, but this
  # workflow's own header rationale for env-hoisting run_id at the
  # commit step (a few lines down) says hardening here should not
  # depend on a guard in a different package — the same reasoning
  # applies to the write, not just the later read. The sibling
  # writes elsewhere in this file (`fault=$rc`, `parse_failed=true`)
  # are NOT touched: they write only shell-local values (a captured
  # numeric exit code, a hardcoded literal), never raw text
  # extracted from the untrusted payload, so the injection class
  # does not apply to them.
  STATUS=$(jq -r '.status // empty' /tmp/ingest-result.json | tr -d '\n\r')
  RUN_ID=$(jq -r '.run_id // empty' /tmp/ingest-result.json | tr -d '\n\r')
  WRITTEN=$(jq -r '.written // empty' /tmp/ingest-result.json | tr -d '\n\r')
  echo "status=$STATUS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "run_id=$RUN_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "written=$WRITTEN" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

# F-f05363e2: on the non-fatal fallback, the inline ::warning:: is the
# only signal — an operator scanning the run SUMMARY page (not the step
# log) sees green with no note that the served README badges are now
# stale. Mirror the 'Warn on stale indexes' step below and also append
# a short note to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY so the degradation is visible on
# the summary. Still non-fatal (a dropped record is worse than stale
# badges); the note carries the self-heal instruction.
node packages/portfolio/generate.js || {
  echo "::warning::badge/trends regeneration failed — the record is still committed by the next step; badges and trends regenerate (and self-heal) on the next ingest."
  echo "### Badge/trends regeneration skipped" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  echo "packages/portfolio/generate.js failed on this run, so the served shields.io badge endpoints (indexes/badges/*.json) and indexes/trends.json were NOT refreshed and may be stale. The ingested record is still committed. Badges regenerate (and self-heal) on the next ingest; to force a refresh now, re-fire any ingest." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
}

git config user.name "dogfood-bot"
git config user.email "64996768+mcp-tool-shop@users.noreply.github.com"
git add records/ indexes/
git diff --cached --quiet && echo "No changes to commit" && exit 0
git commit -m "ingest: ${STATUS:-unknown-status} dogfood record ${RUN_ID:-unknown-run}"

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if git push; then
    echo "::notice::Push succeeded on attempt $attempt for run ${RUN_ID}"
    exit 0
  fi
  # F-68818085: rebase + sleep only when another attempt follows. A
  # rebase after the FINAL failed push can itself hit a conflict, so
  # the run's terminal error would read 'rebase failed during push
  # retry attempt 3' even though no retry was going to happen —
  # misdirecting the operator from the real terminus ('all 3 push
  # attempts failed'). Rebase failures inside the branch still
  # surface immediately rather than continuing the loop with a
  # half-rebased tree: a concurrent ingest touching the same
  # records/ or indexes/ paths produces a merge conflict, and
  # without the guard the next push fails for a different reason
  # with no signal that the underlying issue was a content conflict.
  if [ $attempt -lt 3 ]; then
    wait_s=$((attempt * 10))
    echo "::warning::Push attempt $attempt failed for run ${RUN_ID} — rebasing and sleeping ${wait_s}s before retry"
    git pull --rebase || {
      echo "::error::rebase failed during push retry attempt $attempt — likely concurrent ingest conflict on records/ or indexes/ for run ${RUN_ID}"
      git status --porcelain=v2 || true
      git rebase --abort 2>/dev/null || true
      exit 1
    }
    sleep $wait_s
  fi
done
echo "::error::All 3 push attempts failed for run ${RUN_ID} (no rebase conflict — likely sustained GitHub-API issue or branch protection)"
exit 1

commands.step: Fail run on deferred pipeline fault
commands.text:
rc="${FAULT_RD:-$FAULT_WD}"
echo "::error::ingest pipeline faulted (exit $rc) — see the ingestion step's annotation for the failing stage. Any evidence run.js persisted before the fault was committed above; the run is red because the fault is a genuine pipeline error, not a rejection."
exit "$rc"

commands.step: Fail run on deferred result-parse error
commands.text:
echo "::error::ingest-result.json was not parseable (see the 'Read result' step annotation). The working-tree evidence was still committed above; fix packages/ingest/run.js's stdout contract so it always emits a single JSON object on the result line."
exit 1

if [ -f /tmp/ingest-stderr.log ] && \
   grep -Eq '"failed_stage"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"rebuild_indexes"|may be stale' /tmp/ingest-stderr.log; then
  echo "::warning::indexes/ may be STALE — packages/ingest/run.js persisted the record but the index rebuild failed (it still reported success). The committed record is correct; indexes/ will be rebuilt on the next ingest. To force a rebuild now, re-fire any ingest. See the run.js \"failed_stage\":\"rebuild_indexes\" event below."
  echo "### Stale index warning" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  echo "The record was persisted but the index rebuild failed; indexes/ may be stale until the next ingest. Relevant run.js stderr:" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  grep -E '"failed_stage"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"rebuild_indexes"|may be stale|recovery' /tmp/ingest-stderr.log >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
  echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi

if [ -f /tmp/ingest-result.json ]; then
  echo "### Dogfood Ingestion Result" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  echo '```json' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  cat /tmp/ingest-result.json >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  echo '```' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi
npm ci
node --test scripts/check-accent-color.test.mjs
npm run build

url="$PAGE_URL"
if [ -z "$url" ]; then
  echo "::error::deploy-pages did not emit a page_url output"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Probing $url"
for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  # -L follows redirects (308 trailing-slash enforcement, custom-domain
  # redirects); %{url_effective} surfaces the final URL in the log so a
  # real redirect chain is debuggable without re-running locally. Any
  # 2xx counts as success.
  response=$(curl -sSL -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}" --max-time 15 "$url" || echo "000 -")
  status=$(echo "$response" | awk '{print $1}')
  final_url=$(echo "$response" | awk '{print $2}')
  echo "attempt $attempt: HTTP $status (final: $final_url)"
  case "$status" in
    2*)
      echo "::notice::Pages deploy verified ($url -> $final_url returned $status)"
      echo "page_url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      exit 0
      ;;
  esac
  sleep $((attempt * 5))
done
echo "::error::Pages deploy verification failed — $url never returned 2xx"
exit 1

commands.step: pa11y accessibility check (WCAG2AA, multiple handbook pages with retry)
commands.text:
base="$PAGE_URL"
if [ -z "$base" ]; then
  echo "::error::deploy job produced no page_url output — the a11y job cannot probe an unknown URL. Check the deploy job's verify step."
  exit 1
fi
# Pages probed for WCAG2AA compliance. Curated, not glob-swept, so
# adding a new page is an explicit decision (not a silent regression
# on a new untested page). Update this list when a new high-value
# reference page lands in site/src/content/docs/handbook/.
targets=(
  "${base}handbook/error-codes/"
  "${base}handbook/architecture/"
  "${base}handbook/state-machines/"
  "${base}handbook/cli-reference/"
  "${base}dashboard/"
  "${base}atlas/"
)

cat > /tmp/pa11y-ci.json <<'EOF'
{
  "chromeLaunchConfig": {
    "args": ["--no-sandbox", "--disable-setuid-sandbox"]
  }
}
EOF

failures=()
for target in "${targets[@]}"; do
  echo ""
  echo "::group::pa11y → $target"
  ok=0
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if npx -y pa11y@9.1.1 \
        --standard WCAG2AA \
        --reporter cli \
        --threshold 0 \
        --config /tmp/pa11y-ci.json \
        "$target"; then
      ok=1
      echo "pa11y OK on attempt $attempt: $target"
      break
    fi
    if [ $attempt -lt 3 ]; then
      wait_s=$((attempt * 10))
      echo "::warning::pa11y attempt $attempt failed for $target — sleeping ${wait_s}s before retry"
      sleep $wait_s
    fi
  done
  if [ $ok -eq 0 ]; then
    failures+=("$target")
  fi
  echo "::endgroup::"
done

if [ ${#failures[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::pa11y failed on ${#failures[@]} page(s) after 3 attempts each:"
  for f in "${failures[@]}"; do
    echo "::error::  $f"
  done
  exit 1
fi
echo "::notice::pa11y WCAG2AA OK across ${#targets[@]} handbook pages"

echo "Publishing tag: $PUBLISH_TAG"
git fetch --tags --force
git checkout "$PUBLISH_TAG"
git rev-parse HEAD

commands.step: Install npm >=11.5 in sandbox for OIDC trusted publishing
commands.text:
# Node 22 bundles npm 10.9 which can sign Sigstore provenance but
# cannot negotiate the OIDC trusted-publisher auth path npm added
# in 11.5. In-place `npm install -g npm@latest` races on Node 22's
# bundled npm's own arborist rebuild (MODULE_NOT_FOUND: promise-retry).
# The sandbox shadows system npm via PATH; system npm stays intact.
#
# F-c0348ff6: pinned to an EXACT version (NOT @latest), with
# --ignore-scripts, because this is the only job in the repo that
# holds `id-token: write` (npm OIDC trusted publishing) alongside
# `contents: write`. `npm@latest` resolves whatever npm and
# whatever transitive tree is newest at install time — no
# lockfile, no integrity pin — so any package in that tree could
# run lifecycle scripts inside a job that can mint an OIDC token
# and push to the repo. This mirrors the pa11y exact-version pin
# in pages.yml (npx -y pa11y@9.1.1), which the repo already
# applies to a cosmetic a11y check; the publish job gets the same
# discipline. --ignore-scripts removes arbitrary-code-execution
# from the install itself — the npm CLI needs no lifecycle
# scripts to run from the sandbox's node_modules/.bin. Floor is
# npm >=11.5 for OIDC; 11.5.1 is the first patch release on that
# floor. Bump in lockstep with Dependabot github-actions / npm
# sweeps (same maintenance convention as the pa11y pin).
#
# F-d7fb76ae: this is the FIRST network-dependent step in the
# release job and a hard prerequisite for the entire publish — OIDC
# trusted publishing cannot proceed without it — but pre-fix it had
# zero retry logic, unlike every other network call in this exact
# file (the npm-publish loop below retries 3x with 10s/20s backoff;
# the GitHub Release step tolerates a lost create-race) and its
# sibling workflows (ci.yml's lockfile-drift gate classifies
# ETIMEDOUT/ECONNRESET/etc. as non-blocking; pages.yml's
# deploy-verify curl loop retries 5x and its pa11y step retries
# 3x). A transient registry hiccup on this ONE step failed the
# entire release workflow at its very first step. Bounded impact
# either way — nothing irreversible has happened yet at this point
# (no packages published, no release created), so a bare re-run
# was always a safe recovery; this just makes the retry automatic
# instead of requiring an operator to notice and re-fire.
SANDBOX="$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox"
mkdir -p "$SANDBOX"
pushd "$SANDBOX" >/dev/null
echo '{"name":"npm-cli-sandbox","version":"0.0.0","private":true}' > package.json

ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if npm install --no-save --no-audit --no-fund --silent --ignore-scripts npm@11.5.1; then
    ok=1
    break
  fi
  if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then
    wait_s=$((attempt * 10))
    echo "::warning::npm@11.5.1 OIDC-sandbox install attempt ${attempt} failed — sleeping ${wait_s}s before retry (transient registry/network issue; nothing has published yet, so a retry here is always safe)."
    sleep "$wait_s"
  fi
done
if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "::error::Failed to install npm@11.5.1 into the OIDC sandbox after 3 attempts. Nothing has been published yet (this is the first step of the job) — re-run the workflow once the registry/network issue clears."
  exit 1
fi

popd >/dev/null
echo "$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
"$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin/npm" --version

commands.step: Verify tag matches root package.json version
commands.text:
PKG_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
TAG_VERSION="${PUBLISH_TAG#v}"
echo "Tag: ${PUBLISH_TAG} → ${TAG_VERSION}"
echo "Package: ${PKG_VERSION}"
if [ "${PKG_VERSION}" != "${TAG_VERSION}" ]; then
  echo "::error::Tag ${TAG_VERSION} does not match package.json version ${PKG_VERSION}"
  exit 1
fi

commands.step: Verify every publishable package version matches the tag (lockstep)

commands.text: npm ci
npm run verify

# Carve out the [${TAG_VERSION}] section from CHANGELOG.md.
# awk: print lines from the matching header up to (but excluding)
# the next "## [" header at the start of a line.
TAG_VERSION="${PUBLISH_TAG#v}"
awk -v ver="${TAG_VERSION}" '
  $0 ~ "^## \\[" ver "\\]" { capture=1; print; next }
  capture && /^## \[/ { exit }
  capture { print }
' CHANGELOG.md > /tmp/release-notes.md
# Fail closed if the section was absent (header typo or a forgotten
# CHANGELOG entry): an empty notes file would otherwise cut a release
# with an empty body. -s is true only for a non-empty file.
if [ ! -s /tmp/release-notes.md ]; then
  echo "::error::No CHANGELOG section found for ${TAG_VERSION} — release notes would be empty. Check the '## [${TAG_VERSION}]' header in CHANGELOG.md."
  exit 1
fi
echo "--- release notes preview ---"
head -30 /tmp/release-notes.md
echo "--- (end preview) ---"

commands.step: Publish public packages to npm (idempotent + resilient)
commands.text:
# PB-CI-001: publish each publishable workspace individually so a
# re-fire after a PARTIAL publish (npm 5xx / network blip between two
# packages) is a clean no-op for already-live packages and finishes
# the rest — instead of `npm publish --workspaces` aborting the whole
# step with EPUBLISHCONFLICT on the first already-live package.
#
# For each package:
#   1. `npm view <name>@<version> version` → if it returns the
#      version, the package is already live: skip (idempotency).
#   2. otherwise publish, wrapped in a 3-attempt retry with 10s/20s
#      backoff on transient failure (mirrors the ingest.yml push loop).
#
# Private packages (portfolio) are excluded by reading the same
# non-private filter the version guard uses.
# F-ef512e21: write the enumeration to a file FIRST so the node exit
# code is observable. `mapfile -t PKGS < <(node -e ...)` ignores the
# process substitution's exit status — a corrupt packages/*/package.json
# would leave PKGS empty and this step would fail with the misleading
# 'No publishable packages found' instead of the actual parse error.
# Under `set -e` the plain `node ... > file` form fails the step with
# the real error.
node -e '
  const { readdirSync, readFileSync, existsSync } = require("node:fs");
  const { join } = require("node:path");
  for (const e of readdirSync("packages", { withFileTypes: true })) {
    if (!e.isDirectory()) continue;
    const p = join("packages", e.name, "package.json");
    if (!existsSync(p)) continue;
    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, "utf8"));
    if (pkg.private === true) continue;
    process.stdout.write(`${pkg.name}\t${pkg.version}\n`);
  }
' > /tmp/publishable-pkgs.tsv
mapfile -t PKGS < /tmp/publishable-pkgs.tsv

if [ "${#PKGS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::No publishable packages found under packages/ — nothing to publish. Expected every package under packages/ not marked private."
  exit 1
fi

published=0
skipped=0
for entry in "${PKGS[@]}"; do
  name="${entry%%$'\t'*}"
  version="${entry##*$'\t'}"

  if npm view "${name}@${version}" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "::notice::${name}@${version} already live on npm — skipping (idempotent re-fire)."
    skipped=$((skipped + 1))
    continue
  fi

  ok=0
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    if npm publish -w "${name}" --access public --provenance; then
      echo "::notice::Published ${name}@${version} on attempt ${attempt}."
      ok=1
      published=$((published + 1))
      break
    fi
    # A publish failure may be a race: the package became live between
    # the existence check and the publish (concurrent re-fire). Re-check
    # before retrying so we don't burn attempts on EPUBLISHCONFLICT.
    if npm view "${name}@${version}" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "::notice::${name}@${version} became live during publish (concurrent re-fire) — treating as success."
      ok=1
      skipped=$((skipped + 1))
      break
    fi
    if [ "${attempt}" -lt 3 ]; then
      wait_s=$((attempt * 10))
      echo "::warning::Publish attempt ${attempt} failed for ${name}@${version} — sleeping ${wait_s}s before retry (transient npm/network issue)."
      sleep "${wait_s}"
    fi
  done

  if [ "${ok}" -ne 1 ]; then
    # Fail loud and NAME the package + recovery. Earlier packages in
    # this run are already live and irreversible — a re-fire will skip
    # them (existence check) and resume from here.
    echo "::error::Failed to publish ${name}@${version} after 3 attempts. Already-published packages this run are LIVE and irreversible (compensator: npm deprecate / re-fire to finish). Re-run this workflow to resume — the existence check skips live packages and publishes only the remainder."
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "::notice::Publish summary: ${published} published, ${skipped} already-live/skipped, $(( ${#PKGS[@]} )) total publishable packages."

# --verify-tag asserts the tag exists. If a release already exists
# for this tag (e.g. a re-fire after a partial failure), skip
# creation rather than failing the workflow.
if gh release view "${PUBLISH_TAG}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "GitHub Release ${PUBLISH_TAG} already exists — skipping creation."
  exit 0
fi
# F-60f0c4f5 defense-in-depth: the view-then-create pair above is
# check-then-act. Two concurrent runs for the same tag (now
# serialized by the normalized concurrency group, but belt-and-
# braces) can both pass the view before either creates; the loser's
# create fails AFTER packages are live. Tolerate a lost create race
# by re-checking: if the release exists now, another run created it
# and this is a no-op success, not a red run.
gh release create "${PUBLISH_TAG}" \
  --title "testing-os ${PUBLISH_TAG}" \
  --notes-file /tmp/release-notes.md \
  --verify-tag \
|| {
  if gh release view "${PUBLISH_TAG}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "::notice::GitHub Release ${PUBLISH_TAG} was created by a concurrent run — treating as success."
  else
    echo "::error::gh release create failed for ${PUBLISH_TAG} and no release exists. Packages published this run are LIVE (irreversible); re-fire the workflow to create the release (publish steps are idempotent no-ops)."
    exit 1
  fi
}

npm ci
npm run build

commands.step: Build scenario results from CI conclusion

commands.text:
if [ "${CI_CONCLUSION:-success}" = "success" ]; then
  VERDICT=pass
else
  VERDICT=fail
fi
# The submission is evidence ABOUT the commit CI actually gated. Under a
# workflow_run event $GITHUB_SHA is the DEFAULT-BRANCH head, NOT the
# tested commit — so pin --commit to workflow_run.head_sha, and point
# source.run_url / provider_run_id at the CI run that produced the
# verdict. All three fall back to this run's own env on workflow_dispatch
# (manual re-fire), which has no triggering workflow_run.
COMMIT="${CI_HEAD_SHA:-$GITHUB_SHA}"
RUN_URL="${CI_RUN_URL:-https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
PROVIDER_RUN_ID="${CI_RUN_ID:-$GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
# Build with the LOCAL CLI: self-contained, and it exercises THIS commit's
# builder rather than a published artifact. --precheck runs the SAME
# schema validation the receiver will, so a malformed envelope fails HERE,
# in-workflow, not after a wasted dispatch. Output goes to submission.json
# in $GITHUB_WORKSPACE — the same relative path the Dispatch step slurps
# below (every step shares that working directory).
node packages/report/cli.js \
  --scenario-file scenario-results.json \
  --commit "$COMMIT" \
  --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
  --provider-run-id "$PROVIDER_RUN_ID" \
  --workflow CI \
  --verdict "$VERDICT" \
  --precheck \
  --output submission.json

jq -n --slurpfile s submission.json \
  '{event_type: "dogfood_submission", client_payload: {submission: $s[0]}}' \
  | gh api repos/dogfood-lab/testing-os/dispatches --input -
echo "Dispatched self-submission. Watch ingest: https://github.com/dogfood-lab/testing-os/actions/workflows/ingest.yml"
node packages/report/cli.js --status --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
